title: npm-release-guide project settings (.agents/release.json)
description: Per-project release settings read by the npm-version-guide and npm-publish-guide skills. Top-level publish and versioning are defaults; an entry in packages overrides them for one package folder.

$schema.description: Editor hint. Use the versioned URL of this file.

packages.description: Per-package overrides in a monorepo. npm links Trusted Publishing per package, so each package may name its own workflow and environment.

workflow.description: File name (not path) of the GitHub workflow that publishes through Trusted Publishing; the same value as --file in `npm trust github`.

environment.description: GitHub environment the publishing job runs in; the same value as --env in `npm trust github`.

prereleaseTag.description: Release Tag (npm dist-tag) for Pre-release versions. Not latest (plain installs would get the Pre-release) and not a name npm reads as a version range, such as v1.4 or x (F-89). The release.yml template uses next; change both together.

zeroMajor.description: How 0.x versions bump. minor: a Breaking Change raises the minor number, features and fixes raise the patch number. major: same rules as 1.x and later, so a Breaking Change goes to 1.0.0.

preid.description: Pre-release identifier for new Pre-release lines (the beta in 1.2.0-beta.0). A number must not start with 0 (SemVer).

tagPrefix.description: Prefix of the git tags that already mark this package's releases, used to find the last release. It does not change the tag npm version creates; that comes from npm's tag-version-prefix setting (F-87). In a monorepo, set it in the package's entry to say that these tags belong to that package.

publicInterface.description: Paths or globs, relative to the package folder, that make up the Public Interface. A fix, refactor or perf commit touching them is sent to the Agent for review. Default: the files behind exports, main, module, types and bin.

dir.description: Package folder relative to the folder that holds .agents/, for example packages/core.
